question: How should homosexuals be treated?
summary: Leviticus 20:13 prescribes the death penalty for male same-sex intercourse. 1 Kings 15:11-12 reports Asa simply removing the qedeshim (translated "sodomites" in the KJV) from the land, which reads as exile rather than execution.

reconcile.connective: Defenders deny the two texts even address the same offense: the men Asa removed are the qedeshim, idolatrous shrine prostitutes, not the act Leviticus 20:13 makes capital.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells (Skeptic's Annotated Bible) presses the row as a flat conflict of penalties: Leviticus says such men 'should be killed,' yet righteous Asa merely 'exiled' them from the land.

pd_work.note: Clarke treats this passage directly, glossing the 'sodomites' as הקדשים hakkedeshim, the consecrated/cult figures Asa removed — the harmonizing recategorization keyed to 1 Kings 15:12. Used in place of Haley, whose specific coverage of this exact pair could not be confirmed.

link.title: GotQuestions: Who was King Asa in the Bible?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment that reads Asa's removal of the 'sodomites' (1 Kings 15:12) as the expulsion of male shrine prostitutes tied to Asherah idolatry — the cult-prostitute reading that resolves the tension. Does not cite Lev 20:13 directly but squarely engages the recategorization.

excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Lexically recategorizes the 'sodomites' Asa removed as the qedeshim/consecrated cult figures, not the act criminalized in Lev 20:13 — the move that dissolves the death-vs-exile tension.
